text: Track 7.1 Welcome, Sonja. How do you feel about this decision? Good morning, Tony. It's outrageous! If we waste the money on this art, the health service will be under even more pressure. There's never any spare money for our health service. Surely it would be far better to spend it on providing care for patients and not on art displays that will be better in an art gallery. That's a valid point, Sonja. But isn't art supposed to have health benefits? I'd like to welcome Miranda, who I understand is a street artist to join the debate. I hope that's the right term, Miranda. Hi, Tony. Yes, that's correct. A number of studies on hospital patients have shown that art therapy improves anxiety and reduces pain. In my opinion, it's appropriate to spend £25,000 on artwork with those results. In today's world where everyone is stressed at work and under pressure, we need art therapy more than ever. In fact, I'd suggest spending more if the budget allowed. So, it's money well spent. Good morning, Rosie. What's your view on this? Your daughter is in Drefield hospital at the moment. I hope she's doing well. Hello, Tony. Yes, thank you. She'll be home next week. Right, well, I'm not sure to be honest. I understand the figuring question is a small percentage of their overall budget. Yes, the overall budget is £10 million according to the official report. Right, and I was there last week when they put the artwork up. Some of their contemporary pieces are quite stunning. I love it. I just wonder if children of that age are too young to really appreciate the expensive art they're looking at. That's a good point. Miranda, how would you respond to that? I hear what Rosie is saying about age, and that's true in some ways, but it's not simply about art appreciation in the traditional sense. It's also about communicating with young people and doing that through self-expression. So, you're saying that art can be a method of communication? Yes, artists communicate their attitudes, emotions, and even personalities through their art, which is why art is so diverse and personal. Self-expression and creativity are very important for teenagers, as it teaches them that everyone is different. May I say something here, Tony? Well, perhaps you could just let Miranda finish Sonja, and then you can have your say. You were saying Miranda? Yes, I was getting to the point of art criticism. Children, in this case, those in the hospital ward, like Rosie's daughter, are art critics of the work the hospital has displayed. By considering the value of the art around them, children make decisions about what really matters to them. That is a positive thing, especially at a time when they are unwell. Thank you, Miranda. Very thought-provoking. Sonja? No offense to Miranda, but what is all this nonsense about self-expression? I was shopping in town last week, and the amount of graffiti everywhere was terrible. Most of it is done illegally, I might add. Art has its place, and that is either at school or university or in art galleries. I'm afraid my mind is made up on that point. Well, I'm afraid we have run out of time. As you can see, this is a controversial decision by Drefield Hospital, which I'm sure will continue to debate.
